newsitem.title: USA: Detroit schools hope boxes contain bond documents.
newsitem.headline: Detroit schools hope boxes contain bond documents.

text.p: Detroit Public School officials have uncovered 300 boxes of records that they hope will clear up questions about how proceeds from a 1996 bond issue were spent, the Detroit News reported Wednesday.
The boxes were found at a school vendor's warehouse and contained records covering 1985 to 1993, the newspaper reported.
Questions about the recovered boxes were referred by the school system's press office to William Aldridge, deputy superintendent for finance. Aldridge did not return phone calls.
One school official said it has yet to be determined if records for the $162 million 1986 bond issue are in the boxes.

The lack of an adequate accounting of the bond proceeds led Michigan Treasurer Doug Roberts to refuse to approve any further debt issuance by the school system under the state's school bond loan fund.

In an Aug. 28 letter to Detroit School Supt. David Snead, Roberts said that the school district could only provide 41 out of the 108 expenditure reports related to the 1986 issue that were requested by the treasurer's office.
The Detroit schools had reportedly been planning a $124 million general obligation bond issue, the second such issue to tap into a $1.5 billion GO bonding program approved by voters in 1994.
